html:
The Yanyuwa are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southwest coast of the Gulf of Carpentaria in the Northern Territory, around the McArthur River and the Sir Edward Pellew Islands. Many live today at Borroloola. The map shows them from 1715 to 1800.

They call themselves saltwater people, and their life centred on the sea, the islands and the river mouths, hunting dugong and turtle from canoes. Visiting fleets of the Makassan trepang trade from Sulawesi worked this coast too.

Their language is famous among linguists because men and women speak it differently: nearly every noun and verb has a men's form and a women's form, and children learn both. Neighbours on the map include the Garrwa, the Binbinga and the Waanyi. Cattle stations and a small port at Borroloola came in the 1880s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
